claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic, multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst.
A controlled sub-monolayer of Pd can be deposited on the catalyst surface using ALD.
ALD-deposited Pd will produce a surface-enriched Pd layer.
The surface-enriched Pd layer will form uniform catalytic sites.
The Pd sub-monolayer will promote oxygen activation at low temperatures.
The Pd-modified active sites will be less susceptible to poisoning by H2O and NO.
The Pd sub-monolayer will improve oxygen mobility.
The Pd sub-monolayer will reduce surface degradation during aging.
Adding a Pd sub-monolayer will maintain low overall platinum-group-metal usage.
The Pd-modified catalyst will have a lower CO and hydrocarbon oxidation light-off temperature than the unmodified catalyst.
The Pd-modified catalyst will retain more activity in the presence of H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The Pd-modified catalyst will degrade more slowly during simulated vehicle-lifetime aging than the unmodified catalyst.
The predicted improvements apply under transient exhaust containing CO, hydrocarbons, H2O, and NO at temperatures below 150 °C.
The predicted improvements apply after accelerated thermal cycling and chemical exposure intended to mimic mileage-related degradation.
Earlier studies on Pd-Cu catalysts support the proposed poisoning-resistance and low-temperature-activity mechanism.
Effects outside the specified operating and aging regimes or for different catalyst compositions are not established.
